name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+22 partisan lean anchors the race to Democrats even with Frederica Wilson retiring
Polymarket prices the Democratic nominee at about 96 percent to win
Roughly $2 million in outside spending opposing Oliver Gilbert is notable but unlikely to overcome the seat's fundamentals
No general-election polls or expert ratings, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and markets
model.rationale: This is an open seat in a heavily Democratic-leaning district, and with no polling available the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold. The large outside spending against Gilbert is the only wrinkle, but it is unlikely to move a D+22 seat enough to matter.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Gilbert or an unusually strong Republican candidate could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require a historic shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves this Miami-area seat open, but the district's D+22 partisan lean makes it a strong Democratic hold on paper. Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown and enters as the clear favorite, though outside groups have spent heavily against him.

With no public polling and no expert ratings for the race, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price the Democratic nominee near 96 percent. The expected margin is in the low twenties, with the main uncertainty coming from how the open-seat dynamic and outside opposition play out in a low-information race.
